facts.statement: The report states that digital connectivity is an important driver of growth, productivity and opportunities.
The report states that rural digital connectivity lags urban connectivity.
Gigabit-capable broadband is available to 66% of premises in rural residential areas.
Gigabit-capable broadband is available to 93% of premises in urban residential areas.
The rural-urban gigabit-capable availability gap reported is 27 percentage points.
Approximately 21,218 rural premises in England lack decent broadband via fixed line or fixed wireless access.
Those 21,218 premises represent approximately 0.6% of all rural premises in England.
Cheaper satellite broadband offers have increased the number of consumers able to access decent connectivity.
Ofcom reported about 4,000 residential premises eligible for the broadband Universal Service Obligation as of January 2026.
The report says later market-offer changes may have reduced broadband USO eligibility below Ofcom's January 2026 figure.
63% of rural premises in England have indoor 4G coverage from all four mobile operators.
96% of urban premises in England have indoor 4G coverage from all four mobile operators.
The reported rural-urban gap for indoor 4G coverage from all four operators is 33 percentage points.
Approximately 2% of rural areas have no indoor 4G coverage from any mobile network operator.
Ofcom first reported standalone 5G coverage in its Connected Nations Annual Report 2025.
Standalone 5G was available outside 81% of rural premises in England as of January 2026.
Standalone 5G was available outside 97% of urban premises in England as of January 2026.
The reported rural-urban standalone 5G gap is 16 percentage points.
The report describes reliable high-speed internet as necessary for rural enterprises.
Project Gigabit targets homes and businesses outside suppliers' commercial rollout plans.
The government goal is at least 99% UK gigabit-capable coverage by 2032.
More than 1.3 million rural and hard-to-reach premises had been upgraded through government-funded programmes by the end of December 2025.
The Shared Rural Network met its core objective of 95% geographic 4G coverage from at least one operator one year early.
The report records 35 upgraded Shared Rural Network masts delivering new coverage in England.
